papers.summary: Visual object tracking aims to localize the target object of each frame based on its initial appearance in the first frame. Depending on the input modility, tracking tasks can be divided into RGB tracking and RGB+X (e.g. RGB+N, and RGB+D) tracking. Despite the different input modalities, the core aspect of tracking is the temporal matching. Based on this common ground, we present a general framework to unify various tracking tasks, termed as One Tracker. One- Tracker first performs a large-scale pre-training on a RGB tracker called Foundation Tracker. This pretraining phase equips the Foundation Tracker with a stable ability to estimate the location of the target object. Then we regard other modality information as prompt and build Prompt Tracker upon Foundation Tracker. Through freezing the Foundation Tracker and only adjusting some additional trainable parameters, Prompt Tracker inhibits the strong localization ability from Foundation Tracker and achieves parameter- efficient finetuning on downstream RGB+X tracking tasks. To evaluate the effectiveness of our general framework OneTracker, which is consisted of Foundation Tracker and Prompt Tracker, we conduct extensive experiments on 6 popular tracking tasks across 11 benchmarks and our One- Tracker outperforms other models and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers.authors: Zilong Chen, Feng Wang, Yikai Wang, Huaping Liu
papers.what: [Conference] Automatic text-to-3D generation that combines Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) with the optimization of volume rendering has achieved remarkable progress in synthesizing realistic 3D objects. Yet most existing text-to-3D methods by SDS and volume rendering suffer from inaccurate
papers.summary: Automatic text-to-3D generation that combines Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) with the optimization of volume rendering has achieved remarkable progress in synthesizing realistic 3D objects. Yet most existing text-to-3D methods by SDS and volume rendering suffer from inaccurate geometry, e.g., the Janus issue, since it is hard to explicitly integrate 3D priors into implicit 3D representations. Besides, it is usually time-consuming for them to generate elaborate 3D models with rich colors. In response, this paper proposes GSGEN, a novel method that adopts Gaussian Splatting, a recent state-of-the-art representation, to text-to-3D generation. GSGEN aims at generating high-quality 3D objects and addressing existing shortcomings by exploiting the explicit nature of Gaussian Splatting that enables the incorporation of 3D prior. Specifically, our method adopts a progressive optimization strategy, which includes a geometry optimization stage and an appearance refinement stage. In geometry optimization, a coarse representation is established under 3D point cloud diffusion prior along with the ordinary 2D SDS optimization, ensuring a sensible and 3D-consistent rough shape. Subsequently, the obtained Gaussians undergo an iterative appearance refinement to enrich texture details. In this stage, we increase the number of Gaussians by compactness-based densification to enhance continuity and improve fidelity. With these designs, our approach can generate 3D assets with delicate details and accurate geometry. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, especially for capturing high-frequency components. Our code is available at https://github.com/gsgen3d/gsgen.

papers.summary: We present SplattingAvatar, a hybrid 3D representation of photorealistic human avatars with Gaussian Splatting em-bedded on a triangle mesh, which renders over 300 FPS on a modern GPU and 30 FPS on a mobile device. We disentangle the motion and appearance of a virtual human with explicit mesh geometry and implicit appearance modeling with Gaus-sian Splatting. The Gaussians are defined by barycentric coordinates and displacement on a triangle mesh as Phong surfaces. We extend lifted optimization to simultaneously op-timize the parameters of the Gaussians while walking on the triangle mesh. SplattingAvatar is a hybrid representation of virtual humans where the mesh represents low-frequency motion and surface deformation, while the Gaussians take over the high-frequency geometry and detailed appearance. Un-like existing deformation methods that rely on an MLP-based linear blend skinning (LBS) field for motion, we control the rotation and translation of the Gaussians directly by mesh, which empowers its compatibility with various animation techniques, e.g., skeletal animation, blend shapes, and mesh editing. Trainable from monocular videos for both full-body and head avatars, SplattingAvatar shows state-of-the-art ren-dering quality across multiple datasets. Code and data are available at https://github.com/initialneil/SplattingAvatar.

papers.title: MOSS: Multimodal Origami Swamp Robot System
papers.authors: T. Lan, A. Babgei, L. Romanello, M. Kovac et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Robotic systems for environmental monitoring and ecological surveying in wetlands and swamps must operate across diverse terrestrial and aquatic conditions. Conventional fixed-geometry wheels cannot adapt their contact geometry to these varying conditions. This work presents MOSS
papers.summary: Robotic systems for environmental monitoring and ecological surveying in wetlands and swamps must operate across diverse terrestrial and aquatic conditions. Conventional fixed-geometry wheels cannot adapt their contact geometry to these varying conditions. This work presents MOSS (Multimodal Origami Swamp Robot System), a compact amphibious robotic platform with 3D-printed origami wheels. The compact crank mechanism switches the wheel between contracted and expanded configurations, changing its width, body diameter, and fin orientation simultaneously. The contracted configuration is better suited to efficient rolling on firmer ground, whereas the expanded configuration provides greater contact and terrain engagement on softer surfaces. MOSS was evaluated on soil, sand, mud with varying water content, and water, in addition to in-motion morphing and terrestrial-aquatic transition tests. The more energy-efficient wheel configuration depended on terrain. The contracted configuration achieved a lower cost of transport on firmer soil and mud, whereas the expanded configuration performed better on wetter mud, sand, and water, reducing the cost of transport by up to 29%. Expanded wheels also reduced slip in wet mud and reduced both slip and hub sinkage in sand. MOSS successfully completed configuration changes in $1.95 \pm 0.11$ s and demonstrated continuous locomotion across soil-mud-water transitions. Outdoor trials further demonstrated operation across natural deformable terrain and water. These results show that adaptive wheel geometry provides terrain-dependent locomotion benefits and enables a single compact platform to traverse substantially different terrestrial and aquatic conditions.

papers.title: SparseMax-dSTL: Sound Robustness with Horizon-Independent Gradient Allocation for Temporal Logic Trajectory Optimization
papers.authors: Sai Sandeep Damera, Ryan Matheu, John S. Baras, Calin Belta
papers.what: [Explore] A gradient-based solver that enforces a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification uses a smooth approximation of its quantitative semantics, the robustness. In safety-critical trajectory optimization, this approximation must have two properties. First, it must be sound, that is,
papers.summary: A gradient-based solver that enforces a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification uses a smooth approximation of its quantitative semantics, the robustness. In safety-critical trajectory optimization, this approximation must have two properties. First, it must be sound, that is, nonnegative only on trajectories that satisfy the specification. Second, at each temporal operator, the weight of its gradient on the violating samples must stay bounded away from zero, however long the horizon. The approximations in use, including the log-sum-exp, its sound variant, and the generalized-mean robustness, do not have both. We introduce lower approximations of the minimum and the maximum whose gradients are sparsemax projections, and we prove that the robustness built from them has both. It lies below the exact robustness and is therefore sound, and its error has a bound that is independent of the number of samples and known before optimization. The gradient of each approximation is exactly zero on every sample beyond a data-dependent threshold, so the weight on violating samples a gap beyond the others has a positive lower bound at every horizon. On a planar unicycle and on a seven-joint manipulator beside a person in simulation, the log-sum-exp approximation is positive on a violating trajectory. As the horizon of the manipulator's task grows from 10 to 80 s, the gradient weight of the sound variant on the violating samples falls from 0.22 to 0.04, while that of sparsemax stays at 1. In a constrained trajectory optimization of the unicycle, the constraint on the log-sum-exp robustness returns a violating trajectory, whereas the constraint on the sparsemax robustness returns a trajectory that satisfies the specification with the required margin.

papers.title: "To Boldly Go Where No One Has Gone Before" What Has AI Let Developers Unlock?
papers.authors: Rudrajit Choudhuri, Jenna L. Butler, Christian Bird, Carmen Badea et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Measuring AI by how much faster developers work is like judging electricity by how much faster it spun a steam-era factory. A fuller measure asks what new work becomes possible. We surveyed 331 software developers at Microsoft about what AI lets them do that they could not do bef
papers.summary: Measuring AI by how much faster developers work is like judging electricity by how much faster it spun a steam-era factory. A fuller measure asks what new work becomes possible. We surveyed 331 software developers at Microsoft about what AI lets them do that they could not do before and analyzed their answers using reflexive thematic analysis with a human-in-the-loop, multi-model AI council. Developers described doing familiar work faster (Faster, 45%), undertaking work previously beyond their reach (Further, 36.9%), and taking on new kinds of work centered on building for and directing AI agents (Afresh, 12.4%). Across these accounts, learning and scaffolding ran in both directions: developers learned new skills with AI while externalizing their tacit knowledge as the context and standards that guide AI's work. Drawing on Vygotsky's zone of proximal development, we frame developers and AI as joint learners whose zones meet at the skill-judgment nexus: AI can supply skill faster than it can reliably judge its own work, and developers must continuously bridge that gap. Whether they do sets them on one of two paths. On one, developers' judgment grows alongside AI's skill, and they codify what they learn so the loop keeps turning. On the other, they become hollow orchestrators, approving work they can no longer judge and losing the identity and meaning they once drew from it. Based on our findings, we offer a two-way scaffolding playbook to help developers, teams, and tool builders take the first path.

papers.title: Stationary analysis of adaptive aspiration dynamics in graph-structured games
papers.authors: Dhaker Kroumi
papers.what: [Explore] Aspiration dynamics can favor cooperation on finite graphs through a purely local satisfaction mechanism. papers.summary: Aspiration dynamics can favor cooperation on finite graphs through a purely local satisfaction mechanism. In the model studied here, individuals compare their payoffs with adaptive aspiration levels and revise their strategies through a self-switching Fermi rule. Although the aspirations are continuous and endogenous, the resulting finite-population process has a unique stationary distribution for every finite selection intensity and every finite connected graph under degree-normalized average payoffs when restricted to the compact forward-invariant state space in which aspirations lie in the payoff interval. In the weak-selection regime, the first-order stationary abundance shift is positive when \(R+S>T+P\), negative when \(R+S<T+P\), and zero when \(R+S=T+P\). In the equality case, higher-order terms may determine its direction. The condition \(R+S>T+P\) means that, under neutrality, the expected payoff of a cooperator exceeds that of a defector. The stationary variance reveals a different effect whose first-order correction is governed by the payoff-range contrast \((R-S)-(T-P)\). This contrast compares how strongly cooperator and defector payoffs respond to changes in local neighborhood composition and therefore measures the relative sensitivity of their payoffs to the local environment. Under degree-normalized average payoffs, these first-order results hold on every finite connected graph and are independent of degree sequence, topology, and aspiration learning rate. Simulations on regular and heterogeneous graphs compare averaged and accumulated payoffs and illustrate that graph heterogeneity and the aspiration learning rate can affect stationary behavior away from weak selection. The first-order coefficients are derived from the finite stochastic process and do not use pair approximation, mean-field closure, or a large-population limit.

papers.title: Reusing Calibration Gains across Model Representations
papers.authors: Xu Cao, Wenxuan Xiao
papers.what: [Explore] Scale calibration learns an update for one model representation. We study how much of that update can be reused by another representation of the same pretrained model. Our transfer procedure extracts positive group-wise gains and installs them in the recipient's weights or native
papers.summary: Scale calibration learns an update for one model representation. We study how much of that update can be reused by another representation of the same pretrained model. Our transfer procedure extracts positive group-wise gains and installs them in the recipient's weights or native quantization scales without recipient-side optimization. On a quantized recipient, it preserves integer codes, zero points and storage layout. For a Qwen3-1.7B floating-point/GPTQ INT3 pair, bidirectional transfer retains 76.9-90.5% of the text-loss improvement from recipient-specific calibration on fresh WikiText and C4 cohorts excluded from project development. Shuffling the same gain values within each projection worsens both recipients, showing that their learned group assignment matters after transfer. A Llama-3.2-3B control keeps the initial native tensors at all four calibrated projections identical and changes nine projections elsewhere. Cross-installation retains 98.6-99.3% of the text-calibration benefit, alongside a small, resolved preference for each recipient's own gain. These results quantify both the adaptation carried by a reusable calibration update and the remaining benefit of recipient-specific training.

papers.title: Joining Large String Collections with Jaro-Winkler Similarity
papers.authors: Manuel Lankes, Daniel Kocher, Daniel Schmitt, Willi Mann et al.
papers.what: [Explore] The Jaro-Winkler measure, originally developed for U.S.\ Census record linkage, captures similarities between strings and accounts for common typographical variations. Despite its widespread use, finding all string pairs that exceed a given Jaro-Winkler threshold remains challeng
papers.summary: The Jaro-Winkler measure, originally developed for U.S.\ Census record linkage, captures similarities between strings and accounts for common typographical variations. Despite its widespread use, finding all string pairs that exceed a given Jaro-Winkler threshold remains challenging as the string collection grows large. Existing algorithms for computing the Jaro-Winkler similarity between two strings are either slow for short strings or require quadratic time and fail to scale to long strings. To reduce the number of string comparisons, state-of-the-art techniques perform an index-nested-loop join on trie-based indexes; however, they have only been evaluated on small datasets and high similarity thresholds. For lower similarity thresholds that are relevant in practice, these techniques incur an excessive number of costly Jaro-Winkler computations. We present a novel approach for efficient Jaro-Winkler similarity joins on large string collections. Our solution is based on three key techniques: (1) JUMP is a fast algorithm for computing the Jaro-Winkler similarity between two strings that runs in linear time for bounded alphabets. (2) Dual-bound intersection bitmaps encode strings -- represented as character sets -- into fixed-size bitmaps, which are used to prune candidate string pairs by providing effective bounds on their character overlap; unlike prior bitmap techniques, our bitmaps are equipped with a cost model and adapt to the input data. (3) Our PUMA framework groups strings by prefix to tighten filter conditions, thereby reducing the number of similarity computations. Extensive experiments on large string collections demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms the state of the art, achieving speedups of up to three orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Monitor-Validity Failures: LLM Safety Evidence Paths at Evolving Framework Boundaries
papers.authors: Junchi Liao
papers.what: [Explore] Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs. This creates an interface-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point
papers.summary: Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs. This creates an interface-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point. In one representative case, a regex detector returned a positive match, but the framework stranded the result before the block decision. This differs from jailbreaks and detector errors because the evidence is already recognized yet disconnected from enforcement. We study this repair-boundary signature with canary contracts: parent/fixed confirmation units that place a known payload only on the changed evidence surface and record monitor visibility together with the downstream decision for action-boundary cases. Applying the protocol to public framework repairs, we confirm 18 evidence-path failures across 11 LLM or agent safety project groups and four implementation ecosystems. Nine are established-boundary repairs, eight are new-surface policy-coverage gaps, and one is a boundary-only evidence case. Fourteen reach E1 enforcement boundaries: seven native action outcomes, six configured enforcement boundaries, and one synthetic-consumer consequence. The remaining cases affect verifier, safety-prompt, or observability channels. The cases form carrier, adapter, authority, and surface families and show how ordinary application behavior can remain intact while a safety-specific evidence path misses its decision. Exact revisions, deterministic outcomes, negative controls, and a frozen prospective audit document the confirmation rule. Monitor assumptions therefore need regression tests at the schemas, streams, tools, and adapters that frameworks evolve.

papers.title: Bad Diagnosis: Analyzing Consent and Data Collection Practices of Mobile Medical Apps
papers.authors: Ethan Myers, Lorenzo De Carli, Shantanu Sharma, Ritwik Banerjee et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Mobile health (mHealth) apps collect personally-identifiable information while handling uniquely sensitive medical data, ranging from mental health records to real-time glucose or heart rate monitoring -- yet they remain poorly understood at scale. We present the first comprehens
papers.summary: Mobile health (mHealth) apps collect personally-identifiable information while handling uniquely sensitive medical data, ranging from mental health records to real-time glucose or heart rate monitoring -- yet they remain poorly understood at scale. We present the first comprehensive analysis of consent and data collection practices across 10,000+ mHealth apps on the Google Play Store, combining static analysis and privacy policy examination. We develop a rigorous operational definition to distinguish health apps from general wellness programs, and design a measurement framework to detect misuse of permissions and violations of consent. Our analyses reveal a troubling ecosystem: 69.15% of apps request at least one permission unrelated to their stated purpose, with over 52.9% apps requesting location data, and 50.5% and 34.9% apps requesting camera and microphone access, respectively -- despite no functional justification based on app descriptions and stated purposes. Most alarmingly, nearly 93% of apps fail to provide users with a consent form, directly violating regulatory requirements such as GDPR; and even among the remaining 7%, 1 in 14 demonstrate a gap between the obtained consent and collection of personally identifiable information. These findings demonstrate an urgent need for stronger enforcement of privacy regulations in mHealth apps. We plan to release our dataset and measurement tools for continued monitoring of this critical space.

papers.title: Token-Level Attribution of Multi-Mode LLM Watermarks: Optimal Rule and Belief Weighting
papers.authors: Rui Zhou, Licheng Zhao, Chao Shen, Wenqiang Pu
papers.what: [Explore] A watermark verifier may hold many modes, i.e., secret keys, and a document may mix spans of different modes with unwatermarked text. Directly reporting the mode with the largest pivotal statistic (pivot) inflates the Type I error, and restoring the nominal level reduces power as
papers.summary: A watermark verifier may hold many modes, i.e., secret keys, and a document may mix spans of different modes with unwatermarked text. Directly reporting the mode with the largest pivotal statistic (pivot) inflates the Type I error, and restoring the nominal level reduces power as candidate modes are added. We formulate token-level multi-mode attribution for the Gumbel-max watermark as maximizing correct-label power under a Type I error constraint given a mode prior. We show that the optimal rule reports the mode with the largest prior-weighted alternative density and rejects when this density exceeds one common threshold. Based on this rule, we propose the Belief-weighted Likelihood Attribution with Density Estimation (BLADE) detector. It estimates the mode prior from neighboring pivots and the alternative density from reference token probabilities. Under a conditional product model of the pivots, it keeps the exact Type I error. We further show that BLADE approaches the optimal rule as its prior and density estimates improve, with a sharp coefficient on the density error. On OPT-1.3B and other open-weight large language models, BLADE attains higher correct-label power than the compared detectors across candidate counts, token-substitution rates, generation temperatures and generator models.

papers.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
papers.authors: Antonia Bronars, Younghyo Park, Kushal Kedia, Pulkit Agrawal
papers.what: [Explore] Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. Is joint sensing also enough for precise, contact-rich a
papers.summary: Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. Is joint sensing also enough for precise, contact-rich assembly, where the robot must find a millimeter-scale opening, mesh gear teeth, or catch a thread through light contact? We study this question by training blind assembly policies that observe only a short history of joint positions, velocities, and their own actions, without visual, force, torque, or tactile sensing. The poses of both the fixture and the part are unknown to the policy, and the grasp is randomized substantially. The policy must therefore assemble the parts through contact, sensed exclusively through its own proprioception. Trained with reinforcement learning entirely in simulation over randomized parts, grasps, and contacts, such policies learn peg insertion, gear meshing, and nut threading. The peg insertion policy transfers zero-shot to the real world and inserts pegs of different shapes and sizes in 73% of trials. Controlled comparisons with matched visual policies in simulation show that blind policies generalize far better to unseen part shapes and sizes, though they can be slower. Training such policies needs thousands of different assemblies, each simulated with its clearance intact, so we also release an open-source generator that builds them procedurally from exact convex pieces for MuJoCo; it is more accurate and faster than convex decomposition or MuJoCo's signed-distance collision. Videos and interactive simulations are at https://younghyopark.me/blind-proprioceptive-assembly/.

papers.title: Stochastic Shockwave Dynamics in First-Order Traffic Flow
papers.authors: Yanlin Zhang, Alireza Talebpour
papers.what: [Explore] Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters thro
papers.summary: Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters through the initial spatial density field; every realization follows the same conservation law. For a smooth strictly concave fundamental diagram, we adapt established one-sided spatial Markov closure to traffic variables under the stated spatial-process and regularity assumptions, and derive a kinetic balance for physically normalized front intensities. Evolving the spatial generator provides density laws and congestion-front statistics without solving a road-grid problem for every realization. The formulation is continuous in physical space and time, while its numerical implementation approximates density state and integrates physical time. Four experiments distinguish deterministic consistency from stochastic comparison. Riemann and signal examples recover independently constructed exact LWR solutions. Smooth strictly concave approximations approach the deterministic triangular-diagram signal solution over the tested finite horizons; this does not establish stochastic closure at contacts or the capacity kink. A matched Monte Carlo Godunov ensemble evaluates front counts, sizes, mergers, and density distributions. The evolved generator also yields an instantaneous travel-time distribution for a frozen density field, compared with the same functional of the matched Godunov profiles. This quantity is not experienced travel time through evolving traffic. Resolution checks identify remaining normalization and small-front-loss effects. The contribution is direct evolution and interpretation of traffic-state and front distributions under a fixed first-order traffic law.

papers.title: PrairieFire: Igniting High-Throughput Updates in Large-Scale Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
papers.authors: Yuchen Huang, Baiteng Ma, Yiping Sun, Xiao Chen et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Arrays of modern NVMe SSDs are approaching memory in terms of bandwidth while offering much lower cost per gigabyte. Hence, approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) for billion-scale vectors in applications such as recommendation, search, and retrieval-augmented generation incr
papers.summary: Arrays of modern NVMe SSDs are approaching memory in terms of bandwidth while offering much lower cost per gigabyte. Hence, approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) for billion-scale vectors in applications such as recommendation, search, and retrieval-augmented generation increasingly runs on SSD-based systems. Unfortunately, due to the limited update throughput of existing SSD-based solutions, the indexed corpus cannot keep pace with continuous modifications to data and embedding models, thus hindering broader deployment across more scenarios and larger scales. The bottleneck lies in CPU-intensive update paths, where foreground insertions incur frequent SSD accesses and background reassignments repeatedly relocate each vector, making high update throughput difficult to achieve even by exhausting available hardware. In this paper, using buffered updates and batched local rebuilds, we develop PrairieFire with cascaded adjustments, concurrency control, and CPU-GPU-SSD cooperation. These co-designs avoid frequent SSD accesses in foreground updates and heavy background reassignments, achieving high update throughput while maintaining excellent search performance. Evaluations show that, compared with state-of-the-art systems, PrairieFire can sustain approximately 3-35x update throughput while maintaining approximately 3-5x search throughput simultaneously. It also achieves approximately 1.5-8.7x cost efficiency. PrairieFire has been deployed in RedNote's production environments for two months, improving business metrics by higher freshness without frequent index rebuilds.

papers.title: "Can Computing Systems Eventually Disappear?": A Long-Term Tracking Study on the Use of Diabetes Computing Systems by Patients with Diabetes
papers.authors: Yibo Meng, Jinyuan Zhan, Yao Lyu, Zhuoran Lu et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Ubiquitous computing has long pursued Weiser's vision of technologies that "disappear" into everyday life. As wearable health systems advance, they increasingly substitute for rather than scaffold users' judgment, yet the long-term consequences remain underexplored. We report an
papers.summary: Ubiquitous computing has long pursued Weiser's vision of technologies that "disappear" into everyday life. As wearable health systems advance, they increasingly substitute for rather than scaffold users' judgment, yet the long-term consequences remain underexplored. We report an eight-year, five-wave longitudinal interview study from 2017 to 2025 with 37 patients with diabetes, complemented by interviews with 15 clinicians, designers, and vendors. Across three technological generations including glucometers, continuous glucose monitoring, and predictive and automated insulin delivery systems, we identify a novel user state, continued use with cognitive disengagement. In this state, devices remain in use but active interpretation and questioning recede, leaving users to respond only to alarms. This state emerges from functional expansion, delegation of interpretive authority, and information fatigue, and is reinforced by clinical prioritization, information compression, and automation. It results in less frequent independent health judgment and a shift from understanding to responding. We argue that future diabetes computing systems should reduce unnecessary cognitive work while preserving users' opportunities to interpret, contextualize, and question system outputs.
